title: Lines, angles, triangles and polygons
lines: GRE geometry uses a small set of facts again and again. Learn them well, mark every given value on your scratch paper copy of the figure, and remember that figures are not necessarily drawn to scale unless the question says otherwise.
## Lines and angles
- Angles on a straight line add to 180°. Angles around a point add to 360°. Vertical (opposite) angles are equal.

- When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal, alternate angles are equal, and co-interior angles (same side, between the lines) add to 180°. Every angle formed is one of two values that add to 180°.
> Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and one of the angles is 115°. What are the other seven angles?
> Vertical and corresponding angles equal 115°; the others are 180° − 115° = 65°.
> So there are four angles of 115° and four of 65°.
! Lines that look parallel are not parallel unless the question says so (or arrows mark them). Without that, corresponding angles need not be equal.
## Triangle angles
- The angles of a triangle add to 180°.
- An exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior angles not next to it.
- In an isosceles triangle the angles opposite the equal sides are equal.
> A triangle's angles are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. Find them.
> x + 2x + 3x = 180, so x = 30: the angles are 30°, 60° and 90°.
> An exterior angle of a triangle is 130°, and one of the two remote interior angles is 55°. Find the other.
## Triangle sides
- Triangle inequality: each side is shorter than the sum of the other two and longer than their difference.
- The longest side is opposite the largest angle, and the shortest side is opposite the smallest angle.
> Two sides of a triangle are 5 and 9. The third side is an integer. How many values can it take?
> Integers 5 through 13: that is 13 − 5 + 1 = 9 values.
! The inequalities are strict. A third side of 4 or 14 would make the triangle flat.
## The Pythagorean theorem
- In a right triangle with legs a, b and hypotenuse c: a² + b² = c². The hypotenuse is the longest side, opposite the right angle.
- Common triples and their multiples: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25. A 9-12-15 triangle is 3-4-5 scaled by 3.
- If a² + b² > c² the largest angle is acute; if a² + b² < c², it is obtuse.
> The legs of a right triangle are 9 and 12. Find the hypotenuse.
> 9 = 3 × 3 and 12 = 3 × 4, so the hypotenuse is 3 × 5 = 15. Check: 81 + 144 = 225 = 15².
## Special right triangles
- 45-45-90: sides in ratio 1 : 1 : √2. It is half a square cut along a diagonal.
- 30-60-90: sides in ratio 1 : √3 : 2 (short leg opposite 30°, hypotenuse twice the short leg). It is half an equilateral triangle.
- Equilateral triangle of side s: height (√3/2)s, area (√3/4)s².
> A 45-45-90 triangle has hypotenuse 10. Find each leg.
> A 30-60-90 triangle has short leg 4. Find the other sides.
> Long leg = 4√3 (about 6.93); hypotenuse = 8.
> Find the area of an equilateral triangle with side 6.
## Similar and congruent triangles
- Similar triangles have equal angles and proportional sides. Two pairs of equal angles are enough (AA).
- If corresponding sides are in ratio k, perimeters are in ratio k and areas in ratio k².
- Congruent triangles are identical in size and shape. Tests: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS. SSA and AAA do not prove congruence.
> A pole 2 m tall casts a 3 m shadow while a tree nearby casts an 18 m shadow. How tall is the tree?
> The sun's rays make similar triangles: height/shadow = 2/3 = h/18, so h = 12 m.
> Two similar triangles have corresponding sides 3 and 5. The smaller has area 18. Find the larger area.
> Area ratio = (5/3)² = 25/9, so the larger area is 18 × 25/9 = 50.
! Doubling the sides of a figure doubles the perimeter but multiplies the area by 4. Choices built from "ratio k" for an area are traps.
## Quadrilaterals
- Parallelogram: opposite sides parallel and equal, opposite angles equal, adjacent angles add to 180°, diagonals bisect each other. Area = base × height.
- Rectangle: a parallelogram with right angles; diagonals equal. Square: a rectangle with equal sides; diagonal = s√2.
- Rhombus: four equal sides; diagonals are perpendicular. Area = (d₁ × d₂)/2.
- Trapezoid: one pair of parallel sides. Area = (b₁ + b₂)/2 × h.
> A trapezoid has parallel sides 8 and 14 and height 5. Find its area.
> A rhombus has diagonals 10 and 24. Find its area and side.
> The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making legs 5 and 12, so each side is 13.
! The height of a parallelogram or trapezoid is the perpendicular distance, not the slanted side.
## Polygons
- Sum of interior angles of an n-sided polygon: (n − 2) × 180°. Each angle of a regular polygon: (n − 2) × 180°/n.
- The exterior angles of any convex polygon add to 360°.
> Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 150°. How many sides does it have?
> Each exterior angle is 180 − 150 = 30°, and 360/30 = 12 sides.
> Find the interior angle sum of a hexagon.
> (6 − 2) × 180 = 720°, so each angle of a regular hexagon is 120°.
## Perimeter and area
- Rectangle: P = 2(l + w), A = lw. Triangle: A = (1/2) × base × height, with the height perpendicular to the base (it may fall outside an obtuse triangle).
- For a fixed perimeter, the rectangle with the largest area is a square. Given two sides of a triangle, the area is largest when the angle between them is 90°.
> A rectangle has perimeter 30 and area 56. Find its sides and diagonal.
> l + w = 15 and lw = 56, so the sides are 7 and 8 (7 + 8 = 15, 7 × 8 = 56).
> Two sides of a triangle are 6 and 8. What is the greatest possible area?
> With a right angle between them: (1/2)(6)(8) = 24. Any other angle gives less.
## QC and figure traps
- "Figure not drawn to scale": an angle that looks like 90° may not be. Use only stated facts and what must follow from them.
- Even when drawn to scale, you may trust the order of points on a line and which regions are inside others, not exact lengths.
- Draw the extreme cases. If a triangle could be tall and thin or flat and wide, its area can vary, and the QC answer may be "cannot be determined".
> Triangle sides 6 and 8 with the angle between them unknown. Quantity A: the area. Quantity B: 20.
> The area can be as large as 24 (right angle) or close to 0 (very flat). It can be above or below 20, so the relationship cannot be determined.
## Timing
- Write the formula, then substitute. Most geometry questions need two facts linked together, such as a 30-60-90 triangle inside an equilateral one.
- Use the calculator only to turn a root into a decimal when the choices are decimals.
